quote: Section 14.2 of the Master Supply Agreement provides that any change in direct or indirect ownership of more than 50% of Corbel's voting stock "shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer and shall require the prior written consent of Supplier." If the change occurs without consent, Vantrell may terminate on 30 days' notice. This transaction is a 100% stock purchase and will unambiguously trigger Section 14.2. Yet Disclosure Schedule 4.4 to the SPA states "None" ... Additionally, because Schedule 4.4 lists no consents, the closing condition in SPA § 7.2(c) (all consents on Schedule 4.4 received) is technically satisfied without Vantrell ever being asked.
reason: The memo identifies the issue in substance. It cites Supply Agreement §14.2 as treating a >50% ownership change as an assignment that needs Vantrell's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It states that the 100% stock sale triggers that provision. It explains that the SPA does not cover the consent: Schedule 4.4 says 'None' and the §7.2(c) closing condition reaches only consents listed on that schedule. It also gives the client consequence (Vantrell could terminate the sole-source supply contract after closing) and recommends correcting Schedule 4.4 and making the consent a closing condition.
